stories.title: HKS Adds to Seattle Leadership Team With Addition of Eric Ritchey, Richard Wilson
stories.excerpt: Global design firm HKS announced the addition of two accomplished design leaders to its Seattle office. Eric Ritchey, AIA, joins as Principal and Office Technical Leader, and Richard Wilson, AIA, has been named Vice President and Senior Project Architect in the firm’s Mission Critical Studio. With more than 25 years of experience, Ritchey has built a reputation for leading technically sophisticated projects while aligning multidisciplinary teams around a shared vision. As Office Technical Leader, he will help strengthen technical design excellence across the Seattle practice while supporting project teams in delivering innovative, high-quality solutions. Wilson joins HKS with a diverse portfolio of work across the West Coast, including renovations, tenant improvements, high-density developments and technically complex facilities utilizing wood, steel and concrete construction. A registered architect in Washington, Wilson brings experience leading multidisciplinary teams through all phases of design and construction. Together, the additions of Ritchey and Wilson continue HKS’ investment in growing its Seattle office. The post HKS Adds to Seattle Leadership Team With Addition of Eric Ritchey, Richard Wilson appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HKS adds two senior architects to Seattle office leadership
Ritchey and Wilson bring 25+ years experience in high-density, technically complex design
Signals continued investment in Seattle practice growth and technical capabilities
stories.summary: Design firm HKS expanded its Seattle office by hiring Eric Ritchey as Principal and Office Technical Leader and Richard Wilson as VP and Senior Project Architect. Both architects bring extensive experience in multidisciplinary design, high-density development, and complex construction across the West Coast. The hires reflect HKS's ongoing commitment to grow its Seattle practice and enhance technical excellence.
stories.impact: Marginal relevance to multifamily development. Architect hiring signals Seattle market activity and design-firm appetite for projects, but offers no direct insight into demand, supply, capital, or cost drivers. Talent migration to a market can indicate expected project pipeline, but this is too indirect to act on.

stories.title: Tesla’s Solar Company Seeking Tax Breaks for Fort Bend County Manufacturing Plant
stories.excerpt: Elon Musk and his companies are pretty busy. Yesterday, SpaceX announced plans for a $16.8 billion chip fabrication plant near the Texas A&M campus. And then today, Tesla’s solar battery company filed for tax breaks from Fort Bend County for a potential $10.1 billion solar cell manufacturing plant. The factory would be sited near the intersection of FM 1994 and FM 762 not far from Houston. The Houston Business Journal reports that, in its submittal, the company says the proposed facility would be expected to manufacture photovoltaic solar cells and assemble solar modules, which are components used to convert sunlight into electricity. Operations at the proposed facility would focus on producing finished photovoltaic products for deployment in utility-scale, commercial, and distributed solar installations. The plant would begin operations in 2029. The five land parcels it wants for the project would span more than 3,000 acres. The application asks for a 10-year property tax limitation for the site. The post Tesla’s Solar Company Seeking Tax Breaks for Fort Bend County Manufacturing Plant appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tesla solar subsidiary seeks $10.1B manufacturing plant in Fort Bend County, Texas
3,000+ acre facility near Houston; requests 10-year property tax abatement
Complements SpaceX $16.8B chip fab near Texas A&M; signals massive industrial/energy infrastructure buildup in region
stories.summary: Tesla's solar battery company filed for tax breaks from Fort Bend County to develop a $10.1 billion photovoltaic manufacturing plant spanning 3,000+ acres near Houston. The facility would produce solar cells and modules for utility-scale and commercial deployment. The application seeks a 10-year property tax limitation. This announcement follows SpaceX's simultaneous plan for a $16.8 billion chip fab near Texas A&M.
stories.impact: Major demand tailwind for multifamily in Greater Houston, particularly Fort Bend County and the I-45 corridor. Dual mega-projects (Tesla solar + SpaceX chip fab) will drive population migration, skilled-labor in-migration, and wage growth over 3–5 years; developers should prioritize land acquisition and entitlements in secondary markets within 15–30 miles of these sites before valuations spike. Tax abatements also signal state/local appetite for industrial development, potentially easing regulatory pathways for residential.

stories.title: Sagard Real Estate Acquires Distribution Facility Near Port of Baltimore
stories.excerpt: Sagard Real Estate announced the $91 million acquisition of 7001 Quad Avenue, a 621,144-square-foot distribution facility in Rosedale, Maryland. Located in Baltimore County East, the region’s largest industrial submarket, the asset is fully leased to users across food and beverage distribution and third-party logistics. Built in 2004 on 32 acres, the cross-dock facility is designed for high-volume distribution and features modern industrial specifications. 7001 Quad Avenue is located near the convergence of Interstates 95, 695, and 895, approximately five miles from the Port of Baltimore’s Seagirt and Dundalk marine terminals and downtown Baltimore. The location also provides connectivity to Baltimore/Washington International Airport and the broader Baltimore-Washington corridor. “The building’s cross-dock design, loading capacity and trailer parking support high-throughput operations, while access to the Port of Baltimore and the region’s interstate network will drive sustainable demand from distribution and logistics users over the long term,” said Belah Terentjev, Director, Acquisitions at Sagard Real Estate. bullets: Sagard Real Estate acquires 621K-sf distribution facility in Rosedale, Maryland for $91M
Cross-dock asset built 2004; fully leased to food/beverage and 3PL tenants
Prime location: 5 miles from Port of Baltimore, near I-95/695/895 convergence
stories.summary: Sagard Real Estate paid $91 million for 7001 Quad Avenue, a 621,144-square-foot cross-dock distribution facility in Rosedale, Maryland (Baltimore County East). Built in 2004 on 32 acres, the asset is fully leased to food, beverage, and third-party logistics operators. Its proximity to the Port of Baltimore, interstates 95, 695, and 895, plus Baltimore-Washington International Airport, positions it for sustained logistics demand.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact. This is an industrial acquisition in a logistics-heavy submarket. However, sustained port and logistics activity in Baltimore County East can drive secondary job growth and worker demand in nearby residential markets; multifamily developers should monitor wage and employment trends in the Baltimore-Washington corridor for upside in workforce-housing submarkets 10–20 miles from the port.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow Real Estate sells Hatch Life Sciences building in Long Island City for $86.9M
Asset sold at $5.6M loss vs. 2021 purchase price; $120M value-add plan yielded no premium
Life sciences office market in Queens/LIC softening; financing/exit challenges signal tighter capital
stories.summary: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners sold the Hatch Life Sciences Building in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million—a $5.6 million loss from its $92.5 million 2021 acquisition price with partner Sculptor Real Estate. Longfellow had planned a $120 million renovation into 208,000 sq ft of prebuilt lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office. The sale to Pearl Realty Management suggests difficulty achieving return on the value-add plan in the current market.
stories.impact: Signals stress in life sciences and office market in Queens; multifamily developers should view this as a warning sign on speculative office-to-residential conversion in Long Island City and adjacent submarkets. Buyer appetite for life sciences assets has cooled, and overleveraged sponsors may be forced sellers. Multifamily should avoid aggressive forward-funding for mixed-use projects with office or lab components in NYC until capital markets stabilize and office demand clarifies.

stories.title: Mesa West Capital Originates $52M Refinance for Seattle-Area Apartments
stories.excerpt: Mesa West Capital has provided Timberlane Partners with a $52 million short-term, first-mortgage loan to refinance Sumner Mill Apartments, a 162-unit multifamily community in Sumner, Washington. Delivered in 2024 by the sponsor, Sumner Mill Apartments is a 3.89-acre garden-style community located at 5816 162nd Avenue East with a mix of studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom apartment homes in nine free-standing residential buildings. The financing was arranged by Jake Roberts of BWE in the firm’s Los Angeles office. Located approximately 35 miles south of Seattle and 12 miles east of Tacoma, the city of Sumner benefits from its position as an affordable, family-oriented residential community within commuting distance of both Seattle and Tacoma’s employment centers. “Sumner Mill Apartments achieved stabilization within nine months of delivery and has continued to demonstrate strong leasing momentum,” said Joshua Westerberg, Head of Originations for the Western Region, who led the Mesa West Capital origination team. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. bullets: Mesa West Capital originates $52M refinance for 162-unit Sumner Mill Apartments in Washington
Newly delivered 2024 garden-style community; stabilized in 9 months with strong leasing
Location: 35 miles south of Seattle, 12 miles east of Tacoma; affordable, family-oriented submarket
stories.summary: Mesa West Capital provided a $52 million short-term first-mortgage refinance to Timberlane Partners for Sumner Mill Apartments, a 162-unit garden-style community delivered in 2024 in Sumner, Washington. The asset stabilized within nine months and demonstrated strong leasing momentum. Sumner's position as an affordable residential community between Seattle and Tacoma employment centers attracts families seeking value.
stories.impact: Positive demand signal for secondary/tertiary suburbs in the Seattle-Tacoma market. Fast stabilization (9 months) and strong leasing indicate robust rental demand from workforce commuters; suburban infill and affordable-skewing product remain well-positioned. Developers should focus on similar commuter-shed locations 25–45 miles from core Seattle and Tacoma, where land and construction costs remain favorable relative to urban rents.

stories.title: Berkadia Arranges Recapitalization of MF Within Chicago MSA
stories.excerpt: Berkadia announced the recapitalization of Enclave at 127th, a 340-unit value-add apartment community in Plainfield, Illinois. The transaction was led by Senior Managing Directors Gordon Reynolds and Brian Myers and Vice President Conner Adkins of Berkadia Strategic Capital, in collaboration with Senior Managing Director Pete Evans, Senior Director Richard Evans, and Associate Director Brad Mori of Berkadia Chicago and Berkadia Milwaukee. The sponsor, Chicago-based JVM Realty Corporation, is a vertically integrated, privately owned and operated real estate investment firm. The joint venture equity partner is New York-based DRA Advisors, a real estate investment advisor specializing in value-add investing. JVM will retain ownership through an affiliated investment fund, and the recapitalization positions the partnership to execute its value-add business plan.Conveniently located north of Interstate 55 within the dominant I-55 Industrial Corridor, Enclave is also less than 20 minutes south of Downtown Naperville and the heart of the I-88 Illinois Technology & Research Corridor. bullets: Berkadia arranges recapitalization of 340-unit Enclave at 127th in Plainfield, Illinois
Value-add joint venture between JVM Realty (sponsor) and DRA Advisors; I-55 Industrial Corridor location

The sponsor, Chicago-based JVM Realty Corporation (vertically integrated), partnered with New York-based DRA Advisors in a joint venture equity structure. JVM retained ownership through an affiliated investment fund while the recapitalization provides capital to execute value-add improvements.
stories.impact: Moderate relevance. Shows continued institutional capital appetite for value-add in suburban Chicago, particularly in I-55 corridor (industrial/logistics hub). Proximity to Naperville and supply-chain employment suggests stable workforce demand. Relevant signal: experienced sponsors can still access growth equity without distressed terms; capital markets for stabilizing assets remain open, though rates/terms likely tightened vs. 2021–22.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Capital (Barry Sternlicht) acquires two Miami-Dade affordable housing properties for $63.8M combined
150-unit Magnolia Landing (Naranja): $34M ($226.7K/unit); 160-unit Lafayette Square (Little River): $29.75M ($185.9K/unit)
Freddie Mac financing available; institutional appetite for affordable multifamily in Miami submarket
stories.summary: Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Asset Management acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from Gatehouse Group for a combined $63.8 million. Magnolia Landing in Naranja (150 units, built 2011) sold for $34 million ($226.7K/unit), while Lafayette Square in Little River (160 units, 19-story) sold for $29.75 million ($185.9K/unit). CBRE Capital Partners arranged a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan for Magnolia Landing.
stories.impact: Signals institutional appetite for affordable multifamily in Miami-Dade suburbans and infill neighborhoods. GSE financing (Freddie Mac) remains available for affordable assets, supporting capital formation. Developers should prioritize affordable product in Miami's secondary neighborhoods (Naranja, Little River, Wynwood) where land costs and per-unit pricing remain below Class A core, but demographic trends and transit access create upside. Sternlicht's scale and long-term hold strategy validate these markets for patient capital.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA signs 101K-sf HQ at Hackman Capital's 888 Douglas campus in El Segundo, CA
Agency relocates 590+ employees from Huntington Beach; lease concludes 2027; 50% space expansion
Creative office campus signal: strong employee recruitment value in LA market post-pandemic
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot office lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, near LAX. The company will relocate approximately 590 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction concludes in 2027. The new space will include production facilities for commercials and content, representing a significant expansion and investment in employee experience.
stories.impact: Indirect multifamily signal: strong corporate office leasing and employee relocation in LA metropolitan area suggests sustained job growth and talent migration into Southern California. El Segundo and surrounding beach/airport-adjacent submarkets will see worker demand; multifamily developers should acquire/entitle sites in West LA, El Segundo, Manhattan Beach, and Inglewood (near LAX growth corridors) to capture in-migrating office workers. Demand for workforce housing should materialize 2025–2027 as corporate relocations and expansions land.

stories.title: Attorney James Allen Joins Camber Property Group as Senior Counsel
stories.excerpt: Camber Property Group has onboarded a new general counsel for its affordable housing and community development transactions, Commercial Observer has learned. James Allen has decamped from real estate law firm Hirschen Singer & Epstein and started the new role this week assisting Camber with affordable housing projects in New York state and the New York tri-state region, according to the development firm. “One trend I am seeing is that, in their efforts to solve the ongoing housing affordability crisis, more developers are starting to expand both the types of projects that they participate in and their geographic footprint,” Allen said in a statement. “Camber is always thinking creatively about both, but they present unique challenges.” Allen was previously an associate for four years at Nixon Peabody and a senior staff attorney for the New York Court of Appeals. The Brooklyn Law School graduate also pens articles about housing equity and affordability while serving on the board of the New York Housing Conference’s Rising Leaders Network and the New York City Bar Association’s Housing & Urban Development Committee. Hirschen Singer & Epstein did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “I feel lucky to have the chance to expand upon that and work with many of the legal partners that I have learned from over the years, while Camber solidifies its New York presence and intentionally expands its footprint to other regions,” Allen said. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Camber Property Group hires attorney James Allen as Senior Counsel for affordable housing projects
Focus on NY state and tri-state affordable housing; attorney notes expansion of developer geographic footprint
Trend: developers diversifying project types and markets to navigate housing crisis
stories.summary: Camber Property Group hired attorney James Allen as Senior Counsel to lead affordable housing and community development transactions across New York state and the tri-state region. Allen transitioned from Hirschen Singer & Epstein law firm and brings experience from Nixon Peabody and the NY Court of Appeals. Allen noted a broader industry trend of developers expanding project types and geographic footprint to address the housing affordability crisis.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to for-profit multifamily development. Signals growing market for affordable housing expertise and developer appetite to enter affordable/mixed-income product; if your firm considers affordable or workforce housing, this confirms legal/compliance complexity is rising. Otherwise, this is talent/policy commentary without supply, demand, capital, or cost implications for market-rate multifamily.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Renews 14K-SF 860 Broadway Lease for 10 Years
stories.excerpt: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects has renewed its 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease at Gordon Property Group’s 860 Broadway. Selldorf has called the Flatiron District’s 860 Broadway home for the last two decades, according to landlord brokerage Colliers. The asking rent was not disclosed. However, the average asking rent for office space in Midtown South was $79.41 per square foot, with Class A office space asking an average of $97.22 per foot and Class B space asking $79.96 during the second quarter, according to Colliers data. Seth Hecht from Colliers represented Gordon Property in this deal, while the tenant was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss from Savills. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” Hecht said in a statement announcing the renewal. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” Savills did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment. “Our focus has always been on owning and operating buildings for the long term,” Tim Gordon, managing director of Gordon Property Group, said in the statement. “Creating an environment where great companies choose to stay and grow is the ultimate measure of our success, and we’re proud that 860 Broadway continues to earn that kind of commitment.” Selldorf Architects was founded by Annabelle Selldorf in New York City in 1988, according to the company website. The firm has worked on a number of prestigious projects, including the Frick Collection, the Chateau Haut-Brion — a 16th century estate near Bordeaux in France – and the Museum of Contemporary Art in San Diego. bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 10-year, 13.8K-sf lease at 860 Broadway, Flatiron District, Manhattan
Tenant stability in Class A office; no rent disclosed; market asking avg $79.41/sf (Q2 Midtown South)
Creative/architecture firms anchoring iconic office buildings amid broader office market uncertainty
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 10-year lease for 13,815 square feet at 860 Broadway in Manhattan's Flatiron District, where it has been located for two decades. No rent was disclosed, though Q2 average asking rents in Midtown South were $79.41/sf (Class A: $97.22/sf; Class B: $79.96/sf). The renewal signals tenant confidence in the iconic building and its appeal to creative tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily. Office leasing activity reflects creative-sector stability in Flatiron/Midtown South, but provides no signal on residential demand, supply, or capital trends. Multifamily developers should note that office market in Manhattan remains bifurcated (Class A and creative tenants renewing; Class B/C distressed); no spillover demand for conversion-to-residential is imminent.
